title: Unbalanced window ripple and priority reshuffle playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: During a sustained traffic shift on 2026-01-17 we observed repeated p99+ latency spikes and fairness regressions driven by a feedback loop in the continuous batcher. The batch formation window became unbalanced across worker cohorts, and an adaptive priority reshuffle introduced slot thrashing. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and a concrete playbook for preventing recurrence.
detection_timeline: 2026-01-17 03:12 UTC - Alert: frontend SLOs tripped (p99 generation latency +15%); 2026-01-17 03:14 UTC - Spike correlated to continuous-batcher increase in 'hold' time; 2026-01-17 03:20 UTC - Anomaly: high churn in priority buckets on nodes 4-7; 2026-01-17 03:38 UTC - Rolling throttle experiment initiated; 2026-01-17 04:05 UTC - Short-term rollback of adaptive reshuffle applied; 2026-01-17 05:00 UTC - SLOs recovered to baseline; 2026-01-18 09:00 UTC - Incident review initiated.
impact_summary: Customer visible: transient 2-7x p99 latency spikes affecting conversation generation and streaming tails for ~45 minutes. Internal: scheduled autoscaling mispredicted capacity, costing an additional 120 GPU-minutes. No data loss. Several paid customers reported degraded user experience; incident classified as partial degradation with high customer impact.
root_cause_analysis: Primary contributors: (1) Window imbalance: the adaptive window controller used recent local slot fill rates to expand a cohort's window without global coordination, creating upstream starvation in neighboring cohorts. (2) Priority reshuffle regression: a recent change (PR #GH-2479) that attempted to optimize latency for P0 requests moved requests between buckets more aggressively, causing repeated preemption and slot thrashing. (3) KV cache evictions increased generator warmup costs for rescheduled requests, amplifying the latency impact. (4) Telemetry blind spots: no single metric surfaced the cross-cohort unfairness until p99s were already elevated.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Reverted PR GH-2479 (rollback committed GH-2487) at 2026-01-17 03:24 UTC. 2) Temporarily capped adaptive window growth to +20% per minute cluster-wide. 3) Enabled conservative backpressure on nodes 4-7 to prevent aggressive reshuffle loops. 4) Page rules: if p99 > 2x baseline for >5m, auto-disable adaptive reshuffle. These reduced tail spikes within 40 minutes.
long_term_action_items: Add cluster-coordinated window controller that computes growth based on global fill rates rather than local heuristics - owner: @Diego Morales - due: 2026-03-01
Replace aggressive priority-reshuffle heuristic with stable priority buckets + bounded migration (design doc GH-issue #386) - owner: @Sofia Chen - due: 2026-02-15
Instrument cross-cohort fairness metric (fairness_score = average normalized wait time across priority bands) and add to SLO dashboards - owner: @Aisha Kumar - due: 2026-02-01
Improve KV cache telemetry: expose per-request cold-start count and eviction correlation tags - owner: @Gleb Ivanov - due: 2026-02-10
Add chaos/synthetic test that simulates asymmetric traffic bursts and verifies no cohort p99 regression under 2x baseline - owner: @Reliability Team - due: 2026-02-28
Create automatic rollback playbook and runbook in Console (one-click toggle for adaptive features) - owner: @ProductOps - due: 2026-02-12
